gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same abstract-level universal no-PTAS claim as false: it includes Frobenius-norm minimization despite the paper stating that case is polynomial-time solvable, and it overstates the scope of the established inapproximability results. Its proposed repair directly narrows the abstract claim to the actual exceptions.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The abstract universally asserts NP-hardness and absence of PTAS across the listed criteria, although Frobenius-norm minimization has a polynomial-time exact algorithm and no-PTAS results are not established for every listed criterion.

component_coverage.gold_component: The abstract's universal claim that every listed criterion is NP-hard and admits no PTAS is contradicted by the polynomial-time Frobenius case and exceeds the established results for the other listed criteria.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies both the false universal scope claim and its two substantive reasons: Frobenius minimization is in P, while several listed criteria lack a no-PTAS result. It also proposes the corresponding scope correction.
